title: Relative section cone, supports, and change of topology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on either small site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. An abelian sheaf means a contravariant functor to abelian groups satisfying the sheaf equalizer condition for covering families. For an abelian sheaf $F$ and a nonnegative injective resolution $F	o I^ ullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], put $A^q=I^q(T)$, $B^q=I^q(W)$, $r=\operatorname{res}:A^ ullet	o B^ ullet$, and $K^ ullet=\ker r$. Extend section complexes by zero in negative degrees. Form the relative section complex $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ with $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$, the signed model of $\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $A^ ullet$ and $B^ ullet$ compute derived sections on $T$ and $W$, and the inclusion $K^ ullet	o C^ ullet$, $k\mapsto(k,0)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. It canonically identifies relative cohomology $H^q(C^ ullet)$ with $R^q\Gamma_Z(T,F)$, where $\Gamma_Z(T,F)=\ker(F(T)	o F(W))$, the support convention of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Under this identification the projection $C^ ullet	o A^ ullet$ is forgetting support and the localization boundary is represented by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. These comparisons are independent of resolutions and commute with coefficient morphisms, restriction along etale neighbourhoods, and inclusions $W'\subseteq W$ (enlargement of support). Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For any abelian etale sheaf $F$, the canonical derived-section pullbacks on $T$ and $W$ induce an isomorphism $H^q(T,W;F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}};
u_T^{-1}F)$ for every $q\geq0$, commuting with forgetting support, localization boundary, coefficient morphisms, etale restriction and enlargement of support. Here the pro-etale relative group uses the identical signed section-cone construction. For a pro-etale coefficient morphism $
u_T^{-1}F	o F'$, composition gives the same compatibilities with the supported class in $R^q\Gamma_Z(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F')$.
